I'm not sure what you think is 'older' but I probably qualify. Here are some things I see as better:

Instant delivery: I remember being a kid and ordering things and thinking that the 4-6 weeks delivery time was reasonable. Today, overnight seems like a long time.

Current Information: I learned from books. I had a set of encyclopedias from the year I was born. However, by the time I could read and use the information, a lot of it (most, actually) was out of date. Same with school textbooks, even books we used in school were years (sometimes decades) out of date.

Cars: When I was younger, cars were not nearly so safe, comfortable, reliable or efficient. I drove cars that didn't have seatbelts. Shoulder harnesses didn't come standard in most cars until the 80s (my brother was badly injured in a crash because the car we were in only had lap belts, I wasn't even wearing mine at all). Even if cars had seatbelts, virtually no one wore them (and they were not mandated by law as they are now). And honestly, I'd love to see the IIHS go back and crash test some of the cars from the 70s and 80s. It would be catastrophic. I had a 76 Buick that got about 8-10mpg. Today, my Honda gets 30-35. And being in traffic with old cars without catalytics was horrible. Plus, lots of old cars never had AC.

Phones: No one had mobile phones. If you wanted to call someone, you had to wait until you got home or stop and use a pay phone. No voicemail, if they weren't there you just had to call back. No instant messages, no email. Only regular (snail) mail. And long distance calls outside of your immediate area cost significant money whereas today it's basically free. And oh yeah, pagers. They sucked.

Infrastructure: Most travel was done on surface streets, there were very few major highways or bypasses. No GPS, no voice telling you where to turn. Only paper maps and you had to figure your route for yourself (and not miss a turn)!

There's so much more, but just a few off the top of my head.
